prompt: An example AX3000 product label sums approximately 2,402 and 574 Mbit/s from two radios. A single-link, two-stream Wi-Fi 6 client achieves much less application throughput. Which factors can contribute? Select all that apply.

options.text: The label adds different radios’ maximum PHY rates, while this connection uses one link
options.explanation: Correct. The product aggregate is not the single-link application rate; multi-radio arrangements should not be ruled out merely by generation.

options.text: The phone negotiates a lower MCS (and perhaps 80 MHz rather than 160 MHz) because of distance and walls
options.explanation: Correct. For example, MCS 7 with two streams, 80 MHz and 0.8 µs GI gives roughly 720.6 Mbit/s PHY rate; obstacles alone do not determine this value.

options.text: Per-transmission MAC overhead, half duplex (TCP ACKs share the air) and other stations' airtime
options.explanation: Correct. Protocol overhead, radio-resource sharing and retransmissions affect goodput. There is no universal 50–70% ratio.

options.text: Wi-Fi spends time sending jam signals after every detected collision
options.explanation: Jam signals are CSMA/CD, from wired Ethernet. Wi-Fi cannot detect collisions and never sends jam signals.

options.text: TCP cannot use a window larger than 64 KB, which caps throughput at about 400 Mbit/s
options.explanation: TCP window scaling allows windows far beyond 64 KB, and in any case a 64 KB cap at a few ms RTT would give a different figure. It is not the reason.

workedExample:
Follow the chain from the box to the application:

1. **The label sums two radios.** About 2,402 Mbit/s (5 GHz, 160 MHz, two streams, 1024-QAM) plus about 574 Mbit/s (2.4 GHz) is printed as "3000". A single-link client uses one radio.
2. **The client's own link is slower.** Halving the channel to 80 MHz halves the rate to about 1,201 Mbit/s; a weaker signal that only supports MCS 7 (64-QAM, rate 5/6) brings two streams down to about 720 Mbit/s.
3. **Overhead and sharing.** Contention, preambles, acknowledgments, retransmissions, TCP ACKs on the same half-duplex air and other stations' turns all reduce goodput further. There is no fixed multiplier such as 0.6.

Ethernet jam signals do not exist in Wi-Fi, and TCP window scaling removes any universal 64 KB limit, so options D and E do not explain the gap.
